hints.title: Two-Dimensional Knapsack Constraint Obstacle
hints.text: Each binary string consumes a specific number of zeros and ones, with caps m and n. How can tracking the maximum subset size under dual resource constraints prevent reusing strings?

hints.title: Reverse 2D Capacity Iteration Invariant
hints.text: Traversing capacities backwards from m down to zeros and n down to ones guarantees that each binary string is incorporated into subsets at most once.

hints.title: 2D Array Reverse Fill Procedure
hints.text: Create a 2D table of dimensions (m + 1) x (n + 1) initialized to 0. For each string in strs, count its zeros and ones. Iterate i backward from m down to zeros, and j backward from n down to ones: update table[i][j] to the maximum of table[i][j] and 1 + table[i - zeros][j - ones]. Return table[m][n].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: L: number of strings in strs
complexity.notes: Processes each string with a dual-loop reverse scan over M x N capacity table.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all 2^L subsets causes combinatorial explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: 2D table of size (M + 1) x (N + 1) provides constant space per string step.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using reverse iteration order on both dimensions to enforce 0/1 knapsack semantics.
